title: create the GitHub fork and set origin
description: The upstream merge is done and Sources/Vorssaint is in-tree, but this repo has no origin. Fork vorssaintapp/vorssaint-utils under the user's GitHub account and point origin at it, or decide that origin should be a fresh private repo instead. Needs the user — it creates something under their account.
acceptance_criteria: git remote shows both origin and upstream; the branch pushes; README's attribution names the fork correctly.
close_reason: origin set to github.com/bubblesunyum/control-center-pro (a fork of vorssaint-utils), upstream kept alongside. local branch renamed master -> main to match; merged the one upstream commit the fork was cut ahead of, and pushed. gh CLI is not installed on this machine — the user created the fork themselves.

title: GPLv3 licensing and attribution
description: LICENSE (GPL-3.0-or-later), SPDX headers on every CCP source file, upstream's headers left intact. README states CCP is a fork of vorssaint-utils (c) Vorssaint contributors, GPL-3.0-or-later, with an independent UI and no use of Vorssaint trademarks. Create PATCHES.md as the register for any local upstream patch.
acceptance_criteria: LICENSE present; README carries the attribution and trademark disclaimer; PATCHES.md exists; no Vorssaint name, logo, or icon anywhere in our sources.
close_reason: LICENSE, PATCHES.md, and SPDX headers were already in place from fork setup. Rewrote README as the CCP fork README with Vorssaint attribution, independent-UI statement, trademark disclaimer, and honest in-development framing. Ran verify + local review pass; two correctness findings fixed (engine code is not literally 'unmodified' — deviations tracked in PATCHES.md). Filed ccp-v64: the fork's build.sh still emits a Vorssaint bundle identity (out of scope for this docs bead). Build and tests pass.

title: add CCP targets to Package.swift
description: Add our block to upstream's Package.swift, clearly delimited since it is the known merge-conflict hotspot. Prefer option (a) from the BRIEF: a VorssaintEngines library target over Sources/Vorssaint with App/ and UI/ excluded, so the UI-free boundary is compiler-enforced. Then CCPKit, CCPUI, and the ControlCenterPro executable.
acceptance_criteria: swift build succeeds; VorssaintEngines compiles with App/ and UI/ excluded; deployment target is macOS 14.4; scripts/verify.sh stops skipping the build step.
close_reason: VorssaintEngines library target over Sources/Vorssaint with App/, UI/, main.swift and 38 UI-coupled files excluded; CCPKit/CCPUI/ControlCenterPro/CCPKitTests added; deployment target 14.4. swift build and swift test green, verify.sh no longer skips. Core/Permissions.swift patched (MainActor showGuide hook) rather than excluded — see PATCHES.md. Reviewed by taste + correctness; the showGuide isolation finding was fixed before commit.

title: fork vorssaint-utils and vendor it in-tree
description: Fork vorssaintapp/vorssaint-utils on GitHub, clone it as this repo's history (or graft it in), add the original as an 'upstream' remote. Note: the BRIEF refers to a vorssaint-src clone that is not present in the working tree yet — resolving how upstream's sources land here is part of this task.
acceptance_criteria: git remote shows origin (our fork) and upstream (vorssaintapp/vorssaint-utils); Sources/Vorssaint/ is present and untouched; git fetch upstream succeeds.
close_reason: upstream added as a remote and its history merged with --allow-unrelated-histories; Sources/Vorssaint is in-tree and swift build is green. one conflict (.gitignore) resolved, with upstream's ignores of AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md deliberately dropped and noted in the file. setting origin split out — it needs the user's GitHub account.

title: fork setup and licensing
description: Stand up the fork-based in-tree strategy from BRIEF.md: vorssaint-utils vendored as our engine layer, our targets added alongside, GPLv3 in place from the first commit. Nothing else can start until the package builds.
notes: Reopened 2026-08-29: closed at 4/4 while its acknowledged remainder (fork bundle identity) sat unparented as ccp-v64. v64 is now a child; the epic is 4/5 and stays open until the fork stops shipping a Vorssaint-identified bundle.

title: split CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md — AGENTS.md is bd boilerplate, CLAUDE.md carries everything
description:
AGENTS.md is the untouched bd init file from commit 2f4f71e: generic beads text plus advice about rm -i aliases. CLAUDE.md is 266 lines and shares essentially nothing with it. Any agent reading AGENTS.md — opencode, Codex — never learns the review pass, that scripts/verify.sh is the gate, that Sources/Vorssaint is read-only, the philosophy, naming, animation, accessibility, or the architecture.

Depends on the harness-starter fix (har-32s) landing first: the agent-agnostic half of this content should arrive by install, not be written twice.
design: AGENTS.md takes the harness contract from template/. CLAUDE.md keeps only what is specific to this project: architecture, philosophy, naming, comments, animation, accessibility, testing, upstream rules, build specifics — with a first line pointing at AGENTS.md. The sections already exist; they move. Drop the duplicated beads managed block from CLAUDE.md. Both files get tracks: comments.
acceptance_criteria: An opencode session reading AGENTS.md alone can find the brief, the ledger, the gate, and the review pass, and knows not to edit upstream. Nothing appears in both files.
close_reason: split done: AGENTS.md is the installed harness contract from template/, CLAUDE.md keeps only architecture, philosophy, naming, comments, animation, accessibility, testing and the upstream rules, and imports AGENTS.md so Claude Code still gets the contract. opencode.json installed so the file AGENTS.md names actually exists. Always-loaded cost 4148 → 3818.

title: wire the Dolt transport so the ledger and its memories reach the remote
close_reason: Registered the Dolt remote (bd dolt remote add origin git+https://github.com/bubblesunyum/control-center-pro.git) and pushed. Verified end to end: refs/dolt/data now exists on the GitHub remote, and a fresh clone + bd init + bd dolt remote add + bd dolt pull returned all 37 issues, both memories, and full close reasons — while origin/main was still 4 commits behind, proving the Dolt ref carries the ledger independently of the branch. Both transports now live: jsonl export for git-visible diffs, Dolt for memories/history/merges. Recorded the onboarding sequence as a bd memory. Upstream fixes for the starter are har-nqi (P0), har-l2b, har-jx2, har-xoq, har-638, har-sul.

title: beads never export issues.jsonl — the ledger is invisible to git
description: psymail-mini syncs its ledger by committing .beads/issues.jsonl alongside code; its origin has no refs/dolt/data, so git IS the transport. CCP has no issues.jsonl at all: .beads/config.yaml lacks the 'export: auto: true' block (and sync.remote), so bd never writes the export and every bead filed here is invisible to git and lives only in the local embedded Dolt DB. Root cause is upstream in harness-starter — commands/add.sh runs 'bd init' and stops, and bd's default config ships the export block commented out ('Disabled by default'). psymail-mini's config was hand-edited 3 minutes after its bd init (Aug 10 19:10 -> 19:13); that hand edit is the step the harness extraction never captured.
acceptance_criteria: '.beads/issues.jsonl' exists, is tracked by git, regenerates on bd mutations, and contains the beads filed this session.
close_reason: Added 'sync.remote' + 'export: auto: true' to .beads/config.yaml and generated a clean full .beads/issues.jsonl (37 issues), now tracked in git as of 120a1de. Verified: the export contains this session's beads (ccp-kcc, ccp-459, ccp-v64, ccp-ait, ccp-e2e) and is not gitignored; scripts/verify.sh passed. Root cause is upstream in harness-starter, filed there as har-nqi (P0) with har-xoq/har-638/har-sul. Caveat carried in har-xoq: bd export is incremental and does not drop deleted issues — a full regen (rm issues.jsonl export-state.json && bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl) is the only reliably correct form.

title: README links upstream's docs as CCP's — security reports misroute to Vorssaint
description: The README rewrite (e9cddfb) presents SUPPORT.md, SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and CHANGELOG.md as CCP's docs, but all four are still upstream's, untouched by the fork. SECURITY.md sends vulnerability reports to vorssaintapp/vorssaint-utils/security/advisories/new, so a CCP security report lands in the upstream maintainer's private advisories. SUPPORT.md points bug reports at upstream's issue tracker. CONTRIBUTING.md is titled 'Contributing to Vorssaint' and describes upstream's layout, yet README cites it twice as covering CCP's layout and conventions. CHANGELOG.md is entirely Vorssaint releases with no CCP entries.
design: Rewrite SECURITY.md and SUPPORT.md as CCP's (real consequence, and conflicts on upstream merge are rare and cheap). Do NOT overwrite CONTRIBUTING.md or CHANGELOG.md — they are upstream files that keep receiving upstream commits, and overwriting them makes 'merge upstream/main' expensive, which the fork strategy depends on staying cheap. Relabel those two in the README as upstream's instead.
acceptance_criteria: No README link presents an upstream-authored doc as CCP's own. CCP has its own SUPPORT.md and SECURITY.md routing to bubblesunyum/control-center-pro. Docs that stay upstream's are labelled as upstream's.
close_reason: Rewrote SECURITY.md and SUPPORT.md as CCP's own; security advisories now route to bubblesunyum/control-center-pro with an explicit split for vendored upstream sources. README no longer presents CONTRIBUTING.md/CHANGELOG.md as CCP's — labelled as vendored upstream rather than forked, to keep 'merge upstream/main' cheap. Reviewed by reviewer-taste and reviewer-correctness (both clean, all links and claims verified against the repo); scripts/verify.sh passed. Committed 3d28645.

title: port psymail-mini's durable taste into CLAUDE.md
description: psymail-mini is the same author's macOS menu-bar app and its CLAUDE.md/ARCHITECTURE.md/STYLE.md carry durable taste written for React but meant to transfer to SwiftUI. Translate and port what is relevant, keeping CLAUDE.md's always-loaded cost down by pushing long-form into ARCHITECTURE.md and STYLE.md.
close_reason: taste ported: CLAUDE.md carries philosophy/naming/comments/animation/a11y/testing, long form lives in ARCHITECTURE.md and STYLE.md

title: rename bead prefix con- to ccp-
description: Prefix and every harness reference to it: bd rename-prefix, plus /tmp paths, the commit-msg hook's id pattern, review.sh capture glob, dashboard's bead-id regex, and the skill docs.
close_reason: prefix is ccp- everywhere: config, ids, commit-msg hook, review.sh captures, dashboard regex, verify/brief tmp paths; fixed the last straggler (context.py knowledge-digest path)

title: activate/deactivate lifecycle and idle CPU
description: Sampling runs only while the panel is visible, except for widgets that explicitly opt into background sampling for a menu-bar stat. Enforced through activate()/deactivate(). Engine work off the main thread, models publish on main.
acceptance_criteria: With the panel closed the app measures ~0% CPU over a minute; opening and closing repeatedly does not stack observers or timers; verified with a widget that actually samples.

title: edit mode: wiggle, remove, and drag between lanes
description: Long-press or an Edit button enters edit mode. Widgets wiggle via a small repeating rotationEffect with a random per-item phase offset so they do not sync, show remove badges, and become draggable. Prefer a custom drag gesture plus matchedGeometryEffect over .draggable/.dropDestination, which feel clunky for grid reordering. Drop targets: any position in any lane, plus an empty trailing lane that appears as a target to create a new lane.
acceptance_criteria: Reorder within a lane, move between lanes, and create a new lane by dropping into the trailing slot; layout persists across a relaunch; wiggle phases are visibly unsynchronised.

title: lane layout with placeholder widgets
description: Vertical lanes stacking widget cards, driven by the layout model and rendering whatever the registry provides. Placeholder widgets only at this stage.
acceptance_criteria: Lanes render from a persisted layout across a relaunch; panel width grows with lane count and stops at the screen width.

title: glass card design system
description: The CCPUI vocabulary every widget draws from: spacing scale, corner radii (continuous, ~16-20), thin-material card fill, 1px white-alpha stroke, shadow, type ramp, accent for active toggles. Matches macOS Control Center's language; borrows nothing from Vorssaint, whose design is trademarked.
acceptance_criteria: A widget can be built without a single hardcoded spacing, radius, or colour literal; looks right in light and dark and against a bright and a dark wallpaper.

title: panel dismissal and multi-display behaviour
description: Dismiss on outside click via a global NSEvent monitor, and on Esc. Show on the display holding the status item (or the mouse). The event monitor must be removed when the panel closes — a leaked global monitor is the classic version of this bug.
acceptance_criteria: Outside click and Esc both dismiss; opening and closing 20 times leaves exactly one monitor installed at most; correct display chosen in a two-monitor setup.

title: status item and non-activating glass panel
description: NSStatusItem toggles an NSPanel: .nonactivatingPanel, level .popUpMenu, collectionBehavior [.canJoinAllSpaces, .fullScreenAuxiliary]. Real blur via NSVisualEffectView (.hudWindow or .popover, blendingMode .behindWindow) wrapped for SwiftUI. Anchored top-right of the screen holding the status item, width growing leftward with lane count up to full width. Pre-warm the window at launch.
acceptance_criteria: Panel opens under 100ms perceived; blur is the real thing behind the window, not a material fill; anchoring correct on a second display and with the menu bar auto-hidden.

title: layout model and persistence
description: [Lane] where Lane = [WidgetID], Codable, persisted as JSON in Application Support. Decoding must survive a stored layout naming a widget the registry no longer has, without discarding the rest of the arrangement.
acceptance_criteria: Layout round-trips through JSON; a layout referencing an unknown widget id decodes with that entry dropped and everything else intact; covered by tests.

title: design the CCPWidget protocol and registry
description: Everything hangs off this, so it comes first. CCPWidget with a static WidgetDescriptor (id, title, icon, default size, required permissions), makeView(), activate()/deactivate(), optional settings and compact/expanded variants. Plus WidgetRegistry listing what is available.
acceptance_criteria: A placeholder widget can be declared, registered, and rendered with no change to any other file; unit tests cover registry lookup and descriptor defaults.

title: the shell: panel, lanes, edit mode
description: The glass panel and everything structural around widgets, built with placeholder widgets only. Per BRIEF: get the shell feeling great before wiring any engine.

title: resync harness scripts from harness-starter — opencode-agents.py, .opencode/agent, verify.sh step
description: ccp installed template/AGENTS.md and opencode.json for ccp-veh, but the rest of the harness scripts are behind harness-starter: brief.sh, context.py, review.sh, verify.sh and dashboard.py all differ from the starter's copies, and ccp has no scripts/opencode-agents.py and no .opencode/agent/. The starter's verify.sh runs 'scripts/opencode-agents.py check' as a gate step; ccp's does not, so the reviewers exist only for Claude Code here. Until this lands, an opencode session can read AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md (opencode.json points at both) but cannot run reviewer-taste / reviewer-correctness / reviewer-design.

title: opencode readiness: apply the harness contract here once har-gdz lands
description: Bookkeeping bead for the gate work that landed alongside ccp-veh's prerequisites. The AGENTS.md rewrite itself is ccp-veh and is deliberately NOT done here — template/AGENTS.md should arrive by install once har-gdz adds opencode.json and the generated agents, rather than being hand-written here and diverging.
close_reason: Gate applied, AGENTS.md deduped, both docs blessed. The contract rewrite stays with ccp-veh.

title: migrate the MEMORY.md dashboard note into bd remember
description:
The shared-memory rule now ships in AGENTS.md: bd remember is the durable cross-tool memory because every agent here has bd and the brief already prints the keys, while a tool's own memory stays native and holds pointers.

This repo's memory directory still has the fact rather than the pointer. ~/.claude/projects/-Users-bubbles-dev-control-center-pro/memory/ holds a note that the dashboard opens in Claude Code's browser pane and never the system browser, on port 7393. That is a project fact every session needs and it is invisible to opencode, Codex, and anything else that isn't Claude Code — the exact failure the rule exists to prevent, sitting in the file that documents the rule.
design: bd remember it, leave a one-line pointer in MEMORY.md. Per .claude/HARNESS.md, anything removed from the memory directory is copied to .claude/memory-archive/ and shown to the user first — this is a rewrite rather than a removal, but the archive copy is cheap insurance on the one edit in this project that has no git revert behind it.
acceptance_criteria: bd recall finds the dashboard fact; MEMORY.md keeps a pointer to it and no longer holds the fact itself.

title: drop the duplicate beads managed block from CLAUDE.md
close_reason: Removed the 55-line BEADS INTEGRATION block from CLAUDE.md; AGENTS.md keeps the one copy. Always-loaded cost 4022 to 3342 tokens. The verify.sh guard against a second block reappearing is the harness-starter half, still open on har-7xv.

title: remove the bd prime SessionStart hook and pick up the harness gate for it
bd makes its own git commits, and they bypass the commit-msg hook
description:
Running 'bd dolt remote add' produced commit 815bc9b 'bd: update sync.remote' — authored as the user, not requested, touching .beads/config.yaml (it stripped the trailing newline, nothing more).

Two problems:
1. bd commits to git on its own. This repo's profile is conservative about git actions, and CLAUDE.md says not to commit without authority. A tool that commits as a side effect of a config read/write breaks that expectation silently.
2. The message names no bead. scripts/hooks/commit-msg would reject 'bd: update sync.remote' — the regex needs a ccp- id — so bd is committing with the hook bypassed. That is the same drift ccp-jze was filed for, except the bypass is not a human typing --no-verify, it is a tool doing it invisibly.

Nothing was harmed here; the commit is a one-character whitespace change. The concern is the mechanism.
acceptance_criteria: Either bd's self-commits are disabled, or the hook and the docs acknowledge that bd is a sanctioned committer and its commits are exempt by design rather than by accident.
notes: Found while wiring the Dolt transport (ccp-0t2). Same class of issue as ccp-jze, which removed the --no-verify advertisement from the hook.

title: README build instructions advertise a build that produces a Vorssaint bundle
description: README.md:71-78 tells people to run ./build.sh and ./build.sh --install, but build.sh is upstream tooling that sets EXECUTABLE=Vorssaint and APP_BUNDLE_ID=com.vorssaint.utils (build.sh:27-36). The same README states CCP 'presents no modified build as Vorssaint', and TRADEMARKS.md requires forks to use a different name, icon and bundle identifier. So the README instructs the reader to do the exact thing the README and TRADEMARKS.md forbid. The underlying identity fix is ccp-v64; this bead is the README not advertising it in the meantime.
acceptance_criteria: README does not present ./build.sh as the way to build Control Center Pro without disclosing that it currently produces a Vorssaint-identified bundle, or the instruction is removed until ccp-v64 lands.
close_reason: README's build section now uses 'swift build' and states plainly that build.sh still emits a com.vorssaint.utils bundle TRADEMARKS.md forbids a fork from shipping, pointing at ccp-v64 for the rename. Placeholder clone URL replaced with the real origin. Committed 3d28645.

title: workflow skill staleness gate is blind — context.py picks first tracks comment
description: scripts/context.py:50 uses re.search for '<!-- tracks:' which finds the example comment at .claude/skills/workflow/SKILL.md:108 ('<!-- tracks: … -->') instead of the real tracks at :196. So lock entry is {'…': ''} and none of the 5 real sources (brief.sh, verify.sh, dashboard.py, hooks/commit-msg, context.py) are actually watched — e.g. editing scripts/hooks/commit-msg for ccp-jze did not trigger STALE as it should. Same risk for any doc that mentions tracks: in prose. Fix: make tracked_by find the *last* tracks comment, or anchor to end-of-file, and bless afterwards.

title: CCP's own app bundle still inherits upstream's Vorssaint build identity (build.sh EXECUTABLE=Vorssaint, APP_BUNDLE_ID=com.vorssaint.utils)
description: The fork's build path still produces a Vorssaint-identified bundle: build.sh sets EXECUTABLE=Vorssaint and APP_BUNDLE_ID=com.vorssaint.utils, and Resources/com.vorssaint.utils.fan-control.plist exists. This contradicts the fork's no-Vorssaint-branding position for anything the fork ships. Must rename to Control Center Pro's own identity (bundle id, app name) once the fork has its own identity. Out of scope for the ccp-ait.3 licensing/docs bead; belongs to the fork-setup epic.
notes: Also in scope (same root cause — build.sh has not caught up to the fork): deployment-target mismatch. build.sh:42 sets TARGET=arm64-apple-macosx14.0 and build.sh:409 passes --minimum-deployment-target 14.0, while Package.swift:22 carries the CCP patch to 14.4 (CATapDescription needs 14.4) and the README badge says 14.4+. Raise build.sh to 14.4 alongside the identity rename.

title: ready lane count disagrees with the ready counter
description: dashboard/index.html:1710 rolls child beads into their parent epic's card, so the ready lane draws 4 cards while the header's 'ready to claim' counter says 10 — same word, two denominators. The roll-up is right; the disagreement is what misleads. Either count cards rather than beads in the header, or have the epic card say how many ready children it stands for.

title: commits bypassed the commit-msg hook with --no-verify
description: 3f01781, 6001d7f and ffb9bbc were all committed after 2897fe7 installed a working blocking commit-msg hook, and none names a bead — only --no-verify gets past it. Nothing to backfill without rewriting history. The open question is whether the hook should stop advertising 'git commit --no-verify' in its own refusal text, since that is the line that gets taken. Consider requiring a reason, or logging bypasses so the drift is at least visible.
close_reason: removed the 'Genuinely unfilable? git commit --no-verify' hint from scripts/hooks/commit-msg:39-41 per option #1. Hook now only directs to bd q / bd ready and the required bead id. Verified: blocks missing bead without advertising bypass, passes with ccp-jze, passes fixup!, and scripts/verify.sh passes.

title: PR the Permissions guide hook upstream
description: Core/Permissions.swift is patched locally: two direct calls to PermissionGuideOverlay (a UI/ type) routed through an optional Permissions.showGuide closure, plus a Permissions.GuideKind enum. Small, strictly more flexible than what is there, and costs upstream nothing — they set showGuide to their overlay at startup. Landing it upstream deletes the only real patch in PATCHES.md.
acceptance_criteria: PR opened against vorssaintapp/vorssaint-utils; if merged, the CCP PATCH fences come out of Permissions.swift and the entry leaves PATCHES.md.

title: prove the upstream merge workflow
description: Definition of done requires at least one clean merge upstream/main. Fetch, merge, fix whatever adapters upstream moved, re-verify the VorssaintEngines exclude list still compiles, and write the routine down. Per the BRIEF: always check with the user before updating upstream.
acceptance_criteria: One merge upstream/main completed with the build green afterwards; the routine and its conflict hotspots documented in CLAUDE.md or PATCHES.md.

title: signing and entitlements for audio process taps
description: Process taps need proper signing and audio-capture-adjacent entitlements. Check upstream's build.sh for how they sign and bundle; add an Xcode project or XcodeGen if SwiftPM alone cannot express what signing needs.
acceptance_criteria: A signed .app launches, and the audio adapter can create a process tap on a real machine; the entitlement set is documented in the README.

title: Per-App Audio Mixer widget (Audio adapter)
description: The deepest engine and the one to schedule the most time for: per-app volume via CoreAudio process taps (CATapDescription, macOS 14.4+), plus output/input device switching. Port carefully and mostly intact. Needs the signing and entitlement work to be usable at runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Per-app sliders affect the right process; devices can be switched; taps are torn down on panel close and on device change; missing entitlement surfaces as an inline degraded state rather than a crash.

title: Clipboard History widget (Clipboard adapter)
description: History list with ignored-apps and auto-clear settings over the Clipboard engine. Note this is the one v1 widget that must sample with the panel closed to have any history to show — it is the first real test of the background-sampling opt-out in the lifecycle rules.
acceptance_criteria: History populates while the panel is shut and stays within the configured bound; ignored apps are honoured; clicking an entry copies it back.
notes: BLOCKED ON A UI LEAK: ClipboardHistoryService.swift and ClipboardAutoClearService.swift are excluded from VorssaintEngines because the former names ClipboardQuickPanelView (a UI/ type) at line 1097. Before this widget can be built, that call-site has to be routed around the way Core/Permissions.swift was — see PATCHES.md. One reference, so it should be a small patch plus an upstream PR.

title: Now Playing widget (Media adapter)
description: Now-playing info and transport controls over the Media engine.
acceptance_criteria: Track, artist, and artwork render and update; play/pause/skip work against at least two different players; no polling while the panel is closed.

title: Quick Toggles widget (KeepAwake, Bluetooth, Display)
description: One lane of toggles over three small engines: keep-awake, Bluetooth sleep-toggle, brightness (including external displays, which may need DDC over IOKit) and appearance. Cheap wins that prove the adapter pattern across several engines at once.
acceptance_criteria: Each toggle reflects real system state on open and survives a change made outside the app; external-display brightness either works or degrades visibly rather than silently doing nothing.

title: System Stats widget (Metrics/SystemMonitor adapter)
description: The flagship widget: CPU, memory, temperature, and network graphs over the Metrics and SystemMonitor samplers. Needs VMStatisticsCompat. Adapter exposes an @Observable model; the widget never touches an upstream type.
acceptance_criteria: Live graphs while open, sampling fully stopped when closed; adapter unit-tested against a fake sampler data source.
notes: PARTIAL UI LEAK: SystemMonitor/ProcessUsageService.swift is excluded from VorssaintEngines — it names BreakdownKind, a UI/ type. The other 3 SystemMonitor files and all 16 Metrics files build fine, so the CPU/mem/temp/net graphs are unaffected; only per-process usage needs the leak dealt with. See PATCHES.md.

title: port shared infra from upstream
description: The support layer the widgets lean on: Permissions.swift patterns, HotkeyManager, LaunchAtLogin, Notifier, BoundedProcessRunner, GlobalShortcut, Defaults. Consumed through CCPKit like any other engine — adapters, not edits.
acceptance_criteria: Each is reachable from CCPKit with no import of an upstream type in CCPUI; a permission can be queried and its denial rendered as an inline degraded state.

title: widget gallery for adding widgets
description: The + affordance in edit mode opens a gallery built from WidgetRegistry, showing each descriptor and whether its permissions are satisfied.
acceptance_criteria: Adding from the gallery places the widget and persists; already-placed widgets are indicated; gallery needs no change when a new widget is registered.

title: build, signing, and the upstream merge routine
description: The parts that make the app shippable and the fork sustainable: entitlements and signing for process taps, a smoke test for the gate, and one proven merge upstream/main.

title: v1 widget set
description: The five v1 widgets from the definition of done: System Stats, Quick Toggles, Now Playing, Clipboard History, Per-App Audio Mixer. Each is a CCPKit adapter over an upstream engine plus a CCPWidget conformer.

title: revisit the 38-file exclude list once the shell is real
description: The exclude list in Package.swift was arrived at by iterating swift build until it went green — the second, third and fourth waves are files that fell out behind an earlier exclusion, not files with their own UI coupling. Once ccp-4kq.4 (the Permissions PR) or a similar routing lands, some of them may compile again without their blocker. Worth one pass: try removing the cascade entries and see which stick.
acceptance_criteria: every entry in the exclude list is there because that file itself names a UI type, not because something it depends on was excluded; or the ones that remain are documented as cascade.

title: smoke test for the --full gate
description: scripts/smoke.sh: launch the built app, assert the status item and panel came up, quit. verify.sh --full already calls it when present. This is the only check that can catch a shell that compiles and does not run.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/verify.sh --full runs it and fails when the app fails to launch.
